title: Level unit table
description: How a level's units are named, ordered, and assembled from lesson stems -- read by build-manifest.py's build_curriculum() to generate curriculum.json. One file per level (content/<lang>/curriculum/units/<level>.json), an ordered array of units. Position within a track is this array's own order, not a stored number: two units, or two entries sharing the same `track`, are told apart purely by where they sit in the list. Every level of every course has one (ROADMAP 125), so every unit carries its permanent id; build-manifest.py's auto_group_units() is only a fallback for a brand-new level that has no table yet.

id.description: Permanent unit id (ROADMAP 125, docs/skill-tagging-spec.md § "Vocabulary skills"): one to four English words naming the unit's topic, lowercase and hyphenated, unique within the level across tracks. Set once and never changed, even if the unit moves or its title is reworded -- a unit's position is not its identity. The unit's vocabulary skill is `<level>-<id>-vocab`.

title.description: Human-authored unit name shown in the Learn tab -- not derivable from the stems, so this is the one thing this file exists to carry.

stems.description: Lesson file stems, in teaching order, exactly as they appear on disk under lessons/<level>/ (without the .json extension) -- e.g. "a2-imperfectobasico-01" for lessons/a2/a2-imperfectobasico-01.json. A stem naming a file that doesn't exist yet is fine (build-manifest.py's load_lesson_entry() just skips it), so a unit can be declared before every lesson in it is written.

track.description: Only for a level that runs more than one parallel track (see LEVEL_TRACKS in build-manifest.py, e.g. Spanish B1's Core/Latin America) -- which track this unit belongs to. Omit entirely for a single-track level.

vocabulary.description: Set to false only for a unit with no vocabulary of its own (grammar practice and reading only); such a unit has no <level>-<id>-vocab skill. Omit for every other unit.
